audit.whatIsWrong: The chart gave Skill to level 1, levels 4-5 and level 6, and gave Ornn the 2-item row. The prose says level 1 is his ('he out-ranges you from minute one'), levels 4-5 are his ('this stays his window'), level 6 is 'your one real flip', and at two items it is 'a coinflip on who lands CC first'. The difficulty label is also wrong: this is marked EVEN at 6/10 on a 45.44% win rate over 548 games.
audit.why: Ornn pokes with an 800-range pillar, has a 14s terrain knockup that interrupts Cho'Gath's Rupture wind-up, and gets free item tempo from Living Forge without leaving lane. Cho'Gath's only flip is Feast's true damage against a champion whose entire kit is bonus resistances.
audit.corrected: Ornn / Ornn / Ornn / Ornn / Cho'Gath / Ornn / Skill — matching the packet chart — proposed as one atomic group across win[0..6] and phases[0..6].side+rating, plus diff HARD and diffRating 7/10 to match the win rate.

audit.whatIsWrong: Phase text called Heartsteel Cho'Gath's spike and 'levels 2-3 (full pattern)' his window, and never mentioned the spike that actually exists on Ornn's side.
audit.why: Living Forge is a permanent tempo spike with no recall cost — it is why the first-item row belongs to him — and Call of the Forge God at 140s at rank 1 is the late-game swing. Cho'Gath's single spike is Feast at 6.
audit.corrected: phases[3..6].why rewritten around Living Forge, Feast and Call of the Forge God.

audit.whatIsWrong: The central combo is described wrongly in five fields (spikes[0].text, whys[1], early, mid, wants.foe[0]): they say Searing Charge shatters the Volcanic Rupture pillar 'to apply Brittle', then an empowered auto 'detonates' it. Riot's text puts Brittle on Bellows Breath (W) — 'enemies hit by the final gout of flame become Brittle' — while Searing Charge (E) creates a knockup shockwave when Ornn collides with terrain, which is what his own pillar provides.
audit.why: The player is being told to dodge the wrong ability. The knockup that interrupts Cho'Gath's Rupture wind-up comes from Searing Charge hitting terrain, so the counterplay is positioning away from walls and his pillar; Brittle is a separate cone you dodge separately. As written, a player who sidesteps only the pillar still eats both.
audit.corrected: Brittle reattributed to Bellows Breath and the knockup to Searing Charge colliding with terrain, in spikes[0].text, whys[1], wants.foe[0], wants.you[0], report[5].t, dontsFull[1].d and breakdown.cooldowns.

audit.whatIsWrong: breakdown.cooldowns was placeholder text with no numbers, and it named Volcanic Rupture as the matchup-defining cooldown.
audit.why: The cooldown that decides commits is Searing Charge at 14s at rank 1 — the mid text already says 'only commit when Searing Charge is on cooldown', but no field carried the number. Volcanic Rupture is only 9s and is not the punishing one.
audit.corrected: Searing Charge 14s, Bellows Breath 12s and Call of the Forge God 140s written in.

audit.why: Packet flagged 'Use Living Forge', 'Feral Scream-' and "Feral Scream's" as suspect names. All three are correct names with adjacent punctuation or an ordinary verb — false positives. Recorded so they are not chased again.

notes: The 'mid' and 'late' prose blocks still carry the shattered-pillar-applies-Brittle error ('Feral Scream's silence can stop him from shattering the pillar', 'silence the pillar-shatter with Feral Scream'). Rewriting either inside +/-10% without losing the correct advice around it was not possible in one pass, so they need a second look. NOT ASSERTED anywhere: how Brittle is consumed. Riot's text says only that Bellows Breath makes enemies Brittle and never describes a detonation, an empowered auto, or what Brittle does on being struck — needsResearch is null, so I removed the detonation claims rather than restating them. Also not asserted: whether Feral Scream's silence can interrupt Bellows Breath mid-channel (Riot calls it 'Ornn advances, breathing fire' but does not label it a channel), and whether Searing Charge's knockup can be denied by displacing Ornn first. focus.text reads 'Ornn Volcanic Rupture' with focus.letters ['Q'], which now points at the wrong ability — but focus.text is 21 characters and apply-proposals.js skips strings under 25, so I could not correct it through a proposal and did not flip the letter alone, which would have left the two disagreeing.
